messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueforge.ai>, Elaine Zhou <elaine@blueforge.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: BlueForge discovery — A/B lab sprint & latency/throughput acceptance criteria

Hi Samir / Elaine —

Thanks again for the call today. Helpful to see the production traces you shared (attached) and to understand the latency pain at p95 when the model scales beyond 8 concurrent user streams. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have a single source of truth: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- BlueForge uses a 4096-token context for search+summarization paths; tail latency spikes at p95/p99 on peak workloads.
- Current setup: HyperscalerAlpha endpoints (autoscale to 16 vCPU nodes) for inference and an internal cache layer for hot prefixes.
- Primary objectives for the evaluation: 1) p95 < 250 ms for short responses (<= 128 tokens), 2) p99 reduction relative to HyperscalerAlpha by at least 20%, 3) tokens/sec improvement (measured per worker) for long-context workloads.

Proposed A/B sprint (what Redwood will run vs HyperscalerAlpha):
1) Lab window: next Tue–Thu (Mar 21–23). We run 2 controlled experiments:
   - A: HyperscalerAlpha baseline (you provide trace + external metrics)
   - B: Redwood inference profile (dedicated instance simulating your traffic patterns)
2) Metrics we will capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, median and 95th token/sec (tokens produced/sec), CPU/GPU utilization, KV-cache hit rate, and error/retry counts.
3) Acceptance criteria and primary signals:
   - Short response target: p95 < 250 ms for <=128-token responses
   - Long response throughput: tokens/sec improvement >= 15% at 99th percentile throughput points
   - Stable tail: p99 not higher than HyperscalerAlpha by more than 10%
4) Deliverables: concise A/B report, shared traces, a reproducible harness (k6 + tokenized traces), and a one-hour debrief with your infra team.

As next steps I need from you: 
- Confirm the lab window (we proposed Mar 21–23) and the contact for infra runbook (who can open ports / share ephemeral credentials).
- Share the S3 path for the full sample traces (we got a partial dump on the call).

I attached the partial traces you uploaded during the call and the system spec doc you mentioned. Rafael and Aditya are looped in to scope the test harness and resource sizing.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the lab scheduled.

—
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0126

Attachment stubs:
- blueforge_system_specs.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB, uploaded by BlueForge)
- hyperscaler_alpha_sample_trace.json (JSON, 24 MB, sampled traces)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueforge.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Zhou <elaine@blueforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueForge discovery — A/B lab sprint & latency/throughput acceptance criteria

Monica —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirm we want the lab run next week (Mar 21–23) — that works for our infra and I'll assign Elaine to coordinate the trace share and ephemeral credentials. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Workload shape: the p95 spikes occur when we have 1) many concurrent short requests (avg 32 tokens) and 2) intermittent long-context summarizations (avg 1500 tokens). Can you confirm Redwood will test both shapes separately and also in a mixed workload?
2) For fairness, will Redwood replicate the same autoscale behavior (e.g., same max concurrency per worker) or do you want us to provide a target concurrency table?
3) We have a compliance requirement to never share full user IDs in traces — we will send sanitized traces (user_id hash). Good to know the Redwood team has a private lab environment for this.

We'll upload the sanitized traces to the S3 path by end of day Monday and grant an s3-read-role to aditya.rao@redwood.ai (cc'ing Elaine who will follow up on the IAM details).

Samir
CTO, BlueForge AI
samir.patel@blueforge.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueforge.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueForge discovery — A/B lab sprint & latency/throughput acceptance criteria

Samir / Monica —

I'll own the harness and the lab runs. Quick technical plan and asks so we can minimize back-and-forth when the traces land: 

Planned experiments (detailed):
- W1: Short-response-only run (32-token requests) at 1000 QPS spike ladder (100, 250, 500, 1000 sustained for 60s each). Measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
- W2: Long-context-only run (1500 tokens) with 50 concurrent streams, repeated for 10 minutes, measuring sustained tokens/sec and GPU memory behavior.
- W3: Mixed workload (70% short, 30% long) with bursty arrivals to reproduce tail behavior.

Environment and parity notes:
- We'll run HyperscalerAlpha baseline by replaying their public endpoint behavior (we need the exact request concurrency profile — if you can provide your autoscale/concurrency table that will help parity). If you prefer, we can run a HyperscalerAlpha inside our harness by directing traffic to your existing endpoint (you choose).
- For Redwood runs we'll use the dedicated instance type we discussed (1x A100 equivalent pool, quantization to q4f16 where applicable) — I'll record exact kernel/quant settings in the report.

Data/tools I need from you: 
1) S3 path with sanitized traces + example tokenization map
2) A concurrency/scale table for HyperscalerAlpha endpoints (how many parallel requests per vCPU/node at target sizes)
3) A preferred time window during Mar 21–23 (we can run overnight in our lab if you prefer minimal noisy traffic)

Deliverables from Redwood: 
- Raw results (CSV), consolidated A/B dashboard (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec), harness script (k6 + runner config), and a 30–45 minute debrief.

I'll also attach a small driver (k6 scenario + tokenization helper) to the Drive link so you can review before the run. If there are any constraints (firewall, egress), call them out now.

Thanks — I'll wait for the S3 role and trace upload to schedule the runs.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs referenced:
- redwood_k6_driver.tar.gz (script + config, will be uploaded to shared Drive)
- run_config.template (example concurrency table)
